reply_text:
I found three 2024 candidates that fit your rules. None of them matches the three claims you already have recorded, and I could not confirm any of those three on a page I opened. I ran 10 of the 12 searches and used all 6 page openings.

- **Elad Gil discussion (blog post dated 22 March 2024):** Gil asked when models would beat humans at most office tasks. Mensch said "in three years this is going to look very different". He also said it was "hard to say a date", so this is a weak forecast. The post went up on 22 March; I couldn't confirm the date of the recording itself.
- **McKinsey interview (2 May 2024):** He said work "in three to five years" should be more rewarding because AI tools will take over everyday tasks.
- **French Tech Journal (24 June 2024):** He spoke of "the new industrial revolution that's coming in the next 20 years". This is the journal's English version of what he told the French Senate in May. The span is tied to his point about which companies would capture the value, so it is a marginal fit.

Gaps:
- **5 March 2024 robots claim (on file):** the 22 May 2024 Senate hearing is the likely source. The official Senate record cut off before his section, so I could not quote it. I saw the robots line only in a search-result preview from a Substack (Comptoir IA) summary of the hearing, which I did not open.
- **Other two recorded claims:** the 12 April New York Times interview reached me only through Fortune and Futurism summaries in search results. I found nothing for the 26 March school-agent claim.
- **Partial pages:** the TIME interview (August 2024) cut off partway through. A search preview showed a "Not in the foreseeable future" answer that I couldn't see on the page, so I haven't quoted it. The 20VC podcast transcript (29 April) stopped at about 19 minutes and had nothing usable.
- **Excluded:** his TIME line about staying capital-efficient in 2024–2025 is a business forecast. Nothing about when AGI arrives turned up in 2024.
